newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss econ office sees 1997 GDP up around 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swiss econ office sees 1997 GDP up around 0.5 pct.

text.p: Switzerland's Federal Office for Economic Issues said it expected Swiss real gross domestic product (GDP) to rise around 0.5 percent in real terms in 1997.
"We expect a rise in 1997 GDP of around 0.5 percent," director Hans Sieber told Reuters by telephone from Berne.
"You see a very slow movement out of lasting stagnation," he said. "The main reasons for this are the deep structural adjustments in the quantitatively important (sectors of the) domestic economy."
He said fourth-quarter 1996 data showing GDP stagnated compared with the third quarter indicated that the economy was moving through its trough in the winter semester 1996/97.

"We assume that the second half of 1997 will be better. In particular we expect positive momentum for foreign demand in light of significantly better exchange rates as well as somewhat better economic perspectives in Europe," he said.
This momentum will not be enough, however, to spark a self-sustaining rebound in a domestic economy still undergoing deep structural changes, he added.

"For 1997 we expect only modest overall economic growth, in the first semester continuing stagnation but in the second semester clearly better results. We are emerging from stagnation but one should not be too optimistic."
